messages:
Derek: rolled quant-scheduler v0.3 as a 13% canary at 05:20 UTC. quick bench highlights below.
Maya: ping numbers pls
Derek: short table (canary vs baseline):
```
workload | p50 before -> after | p99 before -> after | cost/token
rwd-7b-chat | 45ms -> 32ms | 210ms -> 178ms | 1.00 -> 0.88
rwd-13b-chat | 70ms -> 53ms | 420ms -> 355ms | 1.00 -> 0.86
short-embed | 28ms -> 20ms | 115ms -> 95ms | 1.00 -> 0.89
```
Ibrahim: nice. what changed in the scheduler?
Derek: groups quantized kernel launches by observed seq-length histogram, primes likely KV prefixes, and does opportunistic small-batch fusion to reduce kernel-launch overhead for short sequences.
Maya: worker/resource impact?
Derek: CPU on canary nodes +8% avg, GPU-util +3%, memory flat. net unit cost down ~11% because fewer queued tokens and fewer kernel launches.
bench-bot: {job: qs-canary-2923, duration_min:50, latency_checks: true, error_rate: 0.12%}
Ibrahim: any regressions or customer-facing errors?
Derek: single 502 during a regional network hiccup, auto-retried by client. health checks otherwise green.
Maya: rollback criteria?
Derek: auto-rollback if p99 > baseline + 35% for >5m OR error_rate >0.5% for >5m. ops playbook includes manual fallback to quant-scheduler v0.2 and a per-tenant mute flag.
Maya: can you prep a 1-slide before/after + exec blurb? also add config snippet to docs.
Derek: exec blurb: "Quant-scheduler v0.3 cut short-seq p50 by ~29% and p99 by ~15% in early canary, reducing unit inference cost by ~11%; staged rollout planned."
deploy-bot: canary-monitoring: next summary in 10m.
Derek: leaving canary watch on. full bench write-up + PR: https://github.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/5102
Maya: awesome work, will include in infra sync if 100% goes green :tada:
